title: Why We Deleted Our MCP Server and Rebuilt It — Abhi Arya, Reducto
talk_summary: Reducto replaced a naive MCP server that exposed every API endpoint as a tool with a smaller set of structured tools that encode workflow patterns, state snapshots, and validators, because agents were confidently wrong and humans couldn't verify outputs. They then made uncertainty legible (confidence scores, explicit ask-user questions, session instrumentation) so failures surface fast and feed back into guidance.

takeaways.technique: Replace API-mirroring tools with workflow-shaped tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one tool per API endpoint, they expose fewer tools that encode known-good multi-step patterns (e.g. a single classify-to-extract tool) so the agent cannot freelance steps the engineers know are correct.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't hand your agent an API, you hand it tools that carry the overall expertise such as the right patterns, the state, and the validators

takeaways.technique: Snapshot tool for live state instead of prompt-stuffed context
takeaways.what_they_do: A single snapshot call returns the live pipeline state including specific error codes, so the agent references real state instead of hallucinating variable names from prompt context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: By moving context out of the prompt and into structure, the agent stopped guessing and started referencing.

takeaways.technique: Fail agents for shaky assumptions; reward asking
takeaways.what_they_do: In evals they penalize the agent for building on unverified assumptions and prompt it to use ask-user/clarification tools instead of guessing when ambiguous.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we started failing the agent for building any shaky assumptions ... We rewarded asking instead of guessing.

takeaways.technique: Surface uncertainty with confidence and reasoning to the reviewer
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent outputs include confidence and reasoning as prompt guidance so the human reviewer can see what was done and why, keeping final judgment accountable with a human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time you make something new, it explains to the user what it did and why, so the user can then review it

takeaways.technique: Instrument agent sessions and feed overrides back into guidance
takeaways.what_they_do: They log every MCP session and prompt, collect where humans overrode the agent or confidence ran low, and fold that back into long-term guidance so the system improves per org.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Where humans overrode the agent, where confidence of the model ran low, and where it asked questions.

takeaways.technique: Keep high-leverage judgment with humans, cheap mistakes early
takeaways.what_they_do: They place agent autonomy where mistakes are cheapest (construction/planning with a human present) and keep final judgment accountable to a human, rather than letting agents run end-to-end unsupervised.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building the pipeline, generating the schema, and pulling in the right context is where the agent is more most powerful and where a mistake is the cheapest
